nodes.summary: The ordinary-value argument needs one exact computation: from five integers $(n,\kappa,a,l,j)$ it must decide whether $r(a,j)$ approximates $n$ to within $\epsilon_l$ and whether $\epsilon_l$ is smaller than an explicit, astronomically small power of four. This chapter turns that computation into rational point-code constraints in two stages. The fixed constants are never evaluated: they enter only through their…
nodes.title: Exact precision computation and polynomial compilation

nodes.summary: The polynomial never manipulates an integer index directly. It represents the index $n$ by the five rational coordinates of the point $[n]P_0$ on an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$, and this chapter proves that the representation is faithful: the canonical codes form exactly the infinite cyclic group $2E(K_0)=\mathbb ZP_0$ (input $\mathsf G$ of the assembly lemma), the membership polynomial recognizes…
nodes.title: The elliptic model of integer indices

nodes.summary: Throughout, $K_0=\mathbb Q(s)$ with $s^2=2$, $d=75-53s$, and $E:y^2=x^3-d^2x$ over $K_0$. For a reduced fraction $a/b$ with $b>0$, $h(a/b)=\log\max(|a|,b)$. In the rank hypotheses and the articles that state them, $d$ instead denotes a positive integer and $C_d$ the congruent number curve $y^2=x^3-d^2x$ over $\mathbb Q$; the row-5b chapter writes $n$ and $C_n$ for these.
nodes.title: The main theorem and its hypotheses

nodes.summary: The target polynomial $P_*$ is defined by construction. It is a finite composition of existential polynomial gadgets: a *template* is a polynomial in parameter and witness variables, a *call* substitutes parameter polynomials and moves the callee's witnesses into a fresh private block of the caller, a sum of squares expresses conjunction over $\mathbb Q$, and a product expresses disjunction. A few astronomically…
nodes.title: The finite specification of the polynomial

nodes.summary: This chapter proves that the rational zero projection of the specified polynomial $P_*$ is exactly $\mathbb Z$, and assembles the target statement. It follows Section 11 of the manuscript (the variable-shift relation for ordinary values) and Lemma 1.2 (assembly).
nodes.title: Assembly and the ordinary-value relation

nodes.summary: The multiplication template is the arithmetic core of the construction: it must accept a triple of rational $5$-tuples exactly when they are the codes $\iota(a),\iota(b),\iota(ab)$ of integer multiples of the generator $P_0$ of $2E(K_0)$. nodes.title: Multiplication and the finite false-triple guard

nodes.summary: This chapter supplies the quantitative half of input B: the fixed constants of the specification are bounded, the guard cutoff $T$ is identified with a closed expression below $2^{2^{2^{9013}}}$, and the specified polynomial $P_*$ is shown to have degree below $2\uparrow\uparrow7$ and coefficients below $2\uparrow\uparrow8$. The constants $D$, $T$, $H_{\rm cat}$, $N_s$, $M_0$, $c_*$, $\ell$ and the program literal…
nodes.title: The cutoff and polynomial size

nodes.summary: The size bounds need every unit class modulo $W=4\prod_{p\le324}p$ to contain twenty-two primes above $324$ below an explicit cutoff. The manuscript takes this from the explicit progression estimate of Bennett, Martin, O'Bryant and Rechnitzer. This chapter proves it instead from an effective form of Dirichlet's theorem with crude but explicit constants: for $q\ge2^{16}$, every unit class modulo $q$ has twenty-two…
nodes.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions

nodes.summary: Route AP replaces the twenty-two-prime pattern by long arithmetic progressions of good slope primes. Szemerédi's theorem in the primes provides them once the good slope primes are known to have positive relative upper density in the primes; this chapter proves that density statement, Proposition D of the route AP note in its weak form, following the project's research note on it. No complex multiplication enters:…
nodes.title: Proposition D: the density of good slope primes

nodes.summary: Route AP replaces the twenty-two-prime pattern by long arithmetic progressions of good slope primes. They come from two theorems: the good slope primes have positive relative density (Proposition D), and every set of primes of positive relative upper density contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length (Green and Tao, Theorem 1.2). This chapter proves the second in Lean. It is the only part of the…
nodes.title: Szemerédi's theorem in the primes (Green–Tao)

nodes.summary: The completeness of the multiplication template needs every integer to be a sum of three good slopes, the slope representation. The manuscript obtains it from the twenty-two-prime pattern of Proposition 6.2, whose proof uses the Green–Tao–Ziegler theory of linear equations in primes. nodes.title: Route AP: progressions of good primes in place of the prime pattern

nodes.summary: The manuscript's pole polynomial puts two points on curves $y^2=x(x-\ell)(x+3\ell)$, and the manuscript derives pole completeness from its restricted converse theorem, whose proof uses Kato's Euler system, Waldspurger's formula, Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein and Nekovář's Selmer complexes. nodes.title: Pole completeness from certified rank (Route K)

nodes.summary: The certified rank hypothesis CR₃ of the main theorem is stated on the explicit linear system $\Sigma(\mathcal C_d)$ of the Route K chapter, built from classes modulo $8$ and Legendre symbols. nodes.title: Proposition 0: the explicit system is the 2-Selmer group

nodes.summary: The forms CR₃^Sel, CR₃^5b, CR₃^TYZ and CR₃^TYZ_Cl of the certified rank hypothesis met so far conclude that every 2-Selmer class of $C_d:y^2=x^3-d^2x$ comes from a rational point, and CR₃ itself that one given class does. nodes.title: The rank hypothesis as positive rank

nodes.title: The row-5b determinant

nodes.summary: For a set $B$ of primes of an odd number $d$, the genus sum $T_{5b}(d)$ of the row-5b chapter uses Rédei's $g_d(B)$, a determinant in the residue bits of the primes. Tian, Yuan and Zhang state their criterion for analytic rank one with the genus class numbers $g(d_B)=|\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d_B}))^2|$ instead, where $d_B=\prod_{p\in B}p$. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
